sections.html:
Central Maryland, between Baltimore and Washington, D.C., is where Howard County sits. Not one incorporated town exists inside it, so the county handles what a city would elsewhere. Columbia, a planned community founded in 1967 with roughly 100,000 residents, and Ellicott City, the county seat with 75,947 residents in 2020, are the names most sellers know.

Median household income was estimated at $124,042 in 2020, and the county school system runs 71 schools for about 49,000 students. With no town layer, a Howard deed goes through one county finance office rather than a town clerk first, which simplifies closing.

Several stream valleys converge on Ellicott City's historic core, which has flooded badly twice. On July 30, 2016 about 6 inches of rain fell in two hours and two people died. On May 27, 2018 more than 8 inches fell in two hours and one person died.

The county's answer was a plan costing roughly $140 million over five years, including a 15-foot-diameter tunnel through about 1,600 feet of hillside. It aimed to bring street flooding down from more than four feet to under one, not to stop flooding altogether. Building removals and construction ran from January 2024 into summer 2024, and renovation of six remaining buildings was still underway in February 2025.

If your house is in or near the historic district, buyers and lenders will ask about flood history and insurance. The same question comes up for homes beside streams elsewhere in the county, so assemble your insurance declarations and any claim records before you list.

sections.h2: Who bills the tax and the rate
sections.html:
Bills come from the county Department of Finance each July 1, while SDAT sets the assessed value. Finance answers at 410-313-2062.

SDAT's 2026 to 2027 table lists a county real property rate of $1.0440 per $100 and a State rate of $0.1120, with a 5% homestead credit cap and no municipal rate. A special rate for services the general rate does not fund can add to the total, so read your own tax account for the full bill.

  • Payment portal: MuniciPay for the current bill.
  • Prior-year bills and history: the county's self-service site.
  • E-check fee: $1.00. Card fee: 2.35%, with a $2.00 minimum.
  • Allow three to five business days for processing.

Many taxpayers can choose semiannual payments. Call Finance to ask which credits you qualify for, and whether any credit on your account ends when you sell. If you are mid-year when the sale closes, the title company usually adjusts the bill between you and the buyer, so having the current amount and payment status in front of you keeps that adjustment accurate. Pay any open balance before listing if you can, since a clean account makes the title search quicker.

To contest a reassessment you must file within 45 days of the notice date. SDAT mails notices on a three-year cycle, which means one arrives every third year and none in between.

Step one is an informal Supervisor's hearing of about 15 minutes. Still unhappy? The local Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board takes appeals filed within 30 days, and the Maryland Tax Court takes them 30 days after the board's order. Neither one costs anything to file.

Between notices, a petition for review can be filed up to the first working day after January 1. A house that transfers after January 1 and before July 1 gives its new owner 60 days from the transfer to appeal.

The Clerk of the Circuit Court's Land Records page lists a State transfer tax of 0.5%, a county transfer tax of 1.25% and a recordation tax of $2.50 per $500 of consideration.

ChargeHoward County amount
State transfer tax0.5% of consideration
County transfer tax1.25% of consideration
Recordation tax$2.50 per $500
Recording fee, 9 pages or less$20
Surcharge on most instruments$40

Every deed goes first to the Division of Recordation Tax, in the Howard County Department of Finance at 3430 Courthouse Drive in Ellicott City, then to Land Records at 9250 Judicial Way, Suite 1900. The recordation office is open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and answers at 410-313-2389. Land Records recording hours are 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

Consideration is not limited to cash and can include debt a buyer assumes. Misstating it on a deed is a crime under the Tax-Property Article.

sections.h2: Overdue tax and the tax sale
sections.html:
One tax sale happens each year, in June, and the Howard County Times carries the list of delinquent properties for at least four weeks first.

Howard has the shortest wait of any county in the state's tax sale report: a property can be offered when it is 30 days overdue. In 2024 the county advertised 1,103 parcels, offered 349 and sold 308, with 173 of those owner-occupied. Interest runs 1.5% a month on the county share and 1% on the State share, and redemption interest is 18% a year.

What bidders purchase is a tax lien certificate, never the house itself. Until a circuit judge signs a foreclosure order, you can redeem. A sale also works, because the payoff on the lien is taken from the proceeds at settlement.

A Howard sale has fewer layers than most, and this order keeps it moving.

  1. Look up your tax account and write down any unpaid balance and special rate.
  2. Get a payoff from Finance through the closing date if tax is overdue, since interest builds monthly.
  3. Agree in the contract on who pays the transfer and recordation taxes.
  4. Take the signed deed to the Division of Recordation Tax first, then to Land Records, or use e-recording.

What to bring to settlement

Have your photo ID, the latest tax bill, your lender's payoff letter if there is a mortgage, and any flood insurance records for a house near a stream. The county says consideration includes more than cash, so tell the title company about any credits or assumed debt so the taxes are figured on the right number. Because the recordation office closes at 4:30 p.m. and Land Records stops recording at 3:30 p.m., plan a same-day closing so the deed gets to both offices in time, or use e-recording to avoid the trip.

If the property needs repairs or has a tax lien, a cash sale as-is can close faster because the buyer is not waiting on a lender's appraisal. The title company still settles the county charges from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When is Howard County property tax billed?
faqs.a: Real property tax is billed on July 1 each year. Many owners can choose two installments, and Finance can confirm the dates on your bill.

faqs.q: How much is the Howard County transfer tax?
faqs.a: Expect 1.25% of the price for the county, 0.5% more for the State, and recordation tax of $2.50 per $500.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Howard County?
faqs.a: Start at the Division of Recordation Tax, 3430 Courthouse Drive, Ellicott City, to pay county taxes and have the deed stamped. Then record at Land Records, 9250 Judicial Way, Suite 1900, or through e-recording.

faqs.q: Do Howard County towns set their own property tax?
faqs.a: No. Howard has no incorporated municipalities, and SDAT lists a municipal rate of 0.0000. All real property tax comes through the county and the State.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal in Howard County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. After the supervisor's hearing the appeals board gives you 30 days, and the Maryland Tax Court another 30 after its order.
